report.source_text: Post-mortem analysis confirmed these findings. Although partially necrotic, the renal mass and extensive metastases involving the retroperitoneum, thorax, and abdominal cavity were noted to have tumor cells with clear cytoplasm. The renal and lung blocks were positive for EMA and CA-IX. A cytology sample from his 4R lymph node biopsy was also reviewed at this time, from which lesional cells were positive for CA-IX and PAX8, with retained expression of FH and SDHB (Fig. 2). These results were most consistent with mccRCC with rhabdoid differentiation.

report.source_text: He was admitted with worsening thrombocytopenia (85 × 109/L) and hypoxia requiring high flow oxygen up to 10 L. He was treated for a pulmonary infection with a broad-spectrum antibiotic regimen, including IV cefepime, IV vancomycin, oral azithromycin, and oral metronidazole. On the third day after his transfer, he suffered cardiac arrest, attributed to respiratory causes, from which he was resuscitated and subsequently intubated. With his clinical status worsening, the decision was made on the third day post-transfer to commence urgent systemic anticancer therapy; he was started on temsirolimus, an mTOR inhibitor, as first-line therapy for presumed metastatic eAML.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old previously healthy man presented to the ED with cough and shortness of breath, initially diagnosed with diffuse bilateral pneumonia and pleural effusion that worsened despite appropriate antibiotic therapy (cefpodoxime, azithromycin) and corticosteroids. Associated systemic symptoms included decreased appetite, mild sinusitis, left lower extremity swelling, and purple toe discoloration. Thoracentesis revealed atypical epithelioid cells. CT imaging identified a 4.7 × 4.7 cm mass in the right kidney lower pole with extensive metastases to retroperitoneal, mesenteric, infracarinal, and hilar lymph nodes. Laboratory findings showed hyponatremia (125 mmol/L), hypoalbuminemia (2.9 g/L), thrombocytopenia (121 × 10⁹/L), mild leukocytosis, and hyperglycemia, with normal renal function and liver tests. After cancer diagnosis, he was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics and temsirolimus (mTOR inhibitor). He suffered cardiac arrest on day 3 post-transfer, was resuscitated and intubated, but clinically declined with worsening ventilation requirements and thrombocytopenia. Goals of care were shifted to comfort measures 10 days after transfer. He died 1 month after initial cancer diagnosis. Autopsy confirmed metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma with tumor cells showing clear cytoplasm, positive for EMA, CA-IX, and PAX8, with retained FH and SDHB expression, consistent with mccRCC with rhabdoid differentiation.
